newsitem.title: UK: Soaring gasoline pushes up Euro petrol pump prices.
newsitem.headline: Soaring gasoline pushes up Euro petrol pump prices.

text.p: Oil companies have raised petrol pump prices in Britain and the Benelux countries as part of a continent-wide drive to match rapidly rising wholesale gasoline values, officials said on Wednesday.
British Petroleum Co. Plc said it had raised its pump prices by two pence a litre in Britain and Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc lifted its wholesale prices by the same amount.
Esso said it would seek to raise its British prices in line with hikes by other suppliers.
Supermarket chain and petrol retailer, ASDA Group Plc, said it would maintain its policy of keeping its petrol prices four percent below the national average.

Oil Price Assessments Ltd, a respected petrol market observer, said Belgian petrol prices were raised on Wednesday by 1.10 francs a litre. Premium unleaded 95 Ron gasoline now costs 38.50 Belgian francs at the pump.
OPAL director Peter Regnier described the rise as the biggest non-tax related pump price hike in Belgium for 25 years.
The Netherlands has seen a two cents rise to 2.24 guilders a litre and Luxembourg also registered a 1.10 franc rise, Regnier said.
An Esso Hamburg spokesman said repeated attempts to raise German pump prices this year had been defeated by fierce competition among suppliers.
But Regnier said German and Dutch pump prices had been raised six times in the past two months, adding that a further Dutch increase was expected by this weekend.
Italian oil firms earlier on Wednesday bowed to government pressure by saying they would freeze pump prices for at least eight days, having on Tuesday announced hikes of five lire a litre.
BP, Shell and Esso all said the British increases were a response to recent strong gains in the international gasoline market.
One British oil company source suggested further hikes might be necessary.
"Two pence is probably not enough. More increases are needed to make up for a $25 a tonne rise in gasoline prices during July alone, so more increases could be in the pipeline," the source said.

The scale of recent wholesale gasoline price gains was underlined earlier on Wednesday by a $240.25 barge deal for prompt premium unleaded gasoline, the highest recorded level since the 1990/91 Gulf War.
British oil majors and petrol retailers have complained of wafer thin margins since Esso introduced its Pricewatch scheme in January 1996.
Continental suppliers have more recently seen their margins squeezed by a combination of rising dollar prices for oil products and rapid gains in the dollar's value against their currencies.
